title: Fabrication of Mechanically Tunable and Bioactive Metal Scaffolds for Biomedical Applications
protocol: Prepare Ti-camphene slurries by mixing commercially available Ti powder, camphene, and KD-4 according to Table 1.
Pour the slurries into 500 ml polyethylene (PE) bottles.
Rotate the bottles at 55 °C for 30 min in a ball-mill oven at 30 rpm.
Pour the slurries from PE bottles into cylindrical aluminum (Al) molds with a diameter of 60 mm and a height of 60 mm.
Seal each Al mold with the corresponding Al cover slip.
Rotate the molds in a ball-mill oven at a speed of 30 rpm at 55 °C for 10 min.
Decrease the temperature of the ball-mill oven to 44 °C.
Continuously rotate the molds at a speed of 30 rpm at 44 °C for 12 hr.
Rotate the molds at room temperature (RT) for 1 hr for cooling process.
Take out the mold from the ball-mill oven after cooling.
Remove the solidified titanium/camphene green body from the Al mold using an Al plunger.
Place the solidified titanium/camphene green body in a rubber bag by hand.
Completely seal the rubber bag by tying the mouth of the bag with a string.
Place the rubber bag in the water tank of a cold isostatic pressing (CIP) machine.
Apply an isostatic pressure of 200 MPa for 10 min.
Remove the compressed green body from the rubber bag.
Transfer the Ti-camphene green body onto an alumina crucible by hand.
Place the crucible in the freeze-dryer machine and freeze-dry at -40°C for 24 hours to sublimate the camphene phase.
Close the crucible with an alumina cover slip.
Place the closed crucible in a vacuum furnace below 10^-6 Torr.
Increase the temperature of the furnace to 1,300 °C at a rate of 5°C/min and hold for 2 hours.
Keep the sintered porous Ti in the furnace until fully cooled to room temperature over 6-7 hours.
Cut the block of sintered porous Ti into disc-shaped samples with a diameter of 16 mm using electrical discharge machining if necessary.
Place the porous Ti samples in a glass beaker and sterilize them at 121°C for 15 minutes in an autoclave.
Remove the samples from the autoclave and wash them twice with distilled water, followed by washing twice with 70% ethanol.
Air-dry the porous Ti samples under UV light on a clean bench at room temperature.
Dilute commercial GFP from 1 mg/ml to 100 μg/ml by mixing 1 ml of GFP with 9 ml of DPBS in a PS tube.
Immerse sterilized dense or porous Ti in 10 ml of diluted GFP solution at RT in a PS tube.
Evacuate the desiccator containing the PS tube for 10 min to enhance GFP penetration into the pores of porous Ti.
Remove the GFP-coated porous Ti from the PS tube using tweezers.
Air-dry the GFP-coated porous Ti overnight at RT on a clean bench.
Rinse the GFP-coated porous Ti twice with DPBS in a glass beaker.
Move the rinsed porous Ti into a 10 cm diameter Petri dish and air-dry at RT on a clean bench.
Place GFP-coated porous Ti samples of various heights in a cylindrical steel die.
Insert punches into the top and bottom holes of the steel die containing the porous Ti samples.
Compress the porous Ti within the steel die assembly at RT in the z direction using a press machine at intermediate strain rates of 0.05 ~ 0.1 sec-1 against predetermined applied strains.
Hold the pressure for 1 min before unloading.
Remove densified Ti samples from the steel die.
Wash the densified samples twice with 10 ml DPBS in a beaker.
Air-dry the samples overnight at room temperature on a clean bench.
Immerse three types of GFP-coated specimens (dense Ti, porous Ti, and densified porous Ti) in 5 ml DPBS solution contained in a sterilized PS tube at 37°C.
Suction out all DPBS from each PS tube with the GFP-coated sample.
Replenish with new 5 ml DPBS solution using a pipette according to predetermined times of 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 15, 22, and 29 days after immersion.
Take fluorescence images of the GFP-coated samples before immersion (day 0) and after 22 day-immersion using confocal laser scanning spectroscopy (CLSM).
Measure the fluorescence signal intensity of the released GFP in 1 ml solution from a total of 5 ml DPBS drawn from each PS tube using UV spectroscopy at 215 nm.
Convert the intensity value into the concentration of the GFP solution using the standard curve.
Draw the standard curve of GFP solution by measuring the fluorescence signal intensity of the GFP solution in the concentration range of 0 ng/ml - 10 μg/ml before measurement.
Machine the sintered porous Ti block according to predetermined structure designs by EDM.
Place the machined Ti samples with height distribution in a steel die where the diameter of porous Ti is approximately 0.1 mm smaller than the diameter of the die.
Insert a set of punches into the top and bottom holes of the steel die.
Measure the mass (ms) of Ti scaffolds.
Calculate the apparent volume (Vs) by measuring length, width, and height of Ti scaffolds.
Compute the porosity using the equation provided.
